summary: Degrade and priority inheritance are unreconciled; PriorityInheritingLock restores a pre-boost priority on unlock so a degrade applied to a boosted holder is silently undone, and degrading a boosted task discards a boost a waiter depends on. INDEPENDENTLY CONFIRMED by the 2026-07-28 external expert audit, which supplied the fix shape this row lacked: replace the stored original_priority restore with a DYNAMIC EFFECTIVE PRIORITY function -- effective = max(base after any degrade, highest waiter priority) evaluated on demand -- so that unlock composes with degrade instead of overwriting it, because the bug is storing a decision that two subsystems can both change

Tcb now holds base_priority (what wcet degrade lowers) and inherited_priority (what lock boost raises), and the priority everything SCHEDULES on is derived as their max on demand, so there is no stored decision left for a second writer to invalidate. The writers are separated by name -- set_base_priority for wcet, inherit_priority and release_inheritance for lock -- and neither can reach the other field. Both orderings now compose: a degrade taken while boosted survives the unlock (the task lands on its floor, not its pre-boost priority) and a degrade applied to a boosted holder does not disturb the boost, so the waiter is not starved by an unrelated overrun.
